explore_lenses.title: A five-year case centered on post-law advocacy
explore_lenses.summary: The prosecution began in September 2021 after the national security law took effect in July 2020. The core legal dispute was whether calls to end one-party dictatorship, expressed through the Alliance's activities and messaging, constituted unlawful incitement to subvert state power.

claims.text: Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan were arrested on September 8, 2021, charged the next day under Articles 22 and 23 of the national security law, denied bail, and the Alliance dissolved later that month.

Hong Kong authorities say the Alliance's objective of ending Chinese Communist Party leadership amounted to overthrowing or undermining China's constitutional system, and that the defendants continued relevant acts after the security law took effect.

UN special-procedure mandate holders said they were concerned that the prosecution and lengthy detention appeared connected to political expression, human-rights work, and pro-democracy activities, and questioned the precision of the alleged conduct under international human-rights standards.
The court said the law was not applied retrospectively and that convictions rested on conduct during the charge period, not on the defendants' ideology or their actions before the law took effect.

story_report.summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced three prominent organizers of annual Tiananmen Square vigils to prison terms of between five years and seven years and three months under the national security law. Chow Hang-tung received the longest term, followed by Lee Cheuk-yan, while Albert Ho received a shorter sentence after pleading guilty. The case centers on the Hong Kong Alliance, which organized the vigils for about three decades, and leaves the three activists facing lengthy imprisonment for conduct linked to the group’s activities after the law took effect.

sections.heading: Hong Kong Alliance Vigil History
sections.body: The Hong Kong Alliance had organized the annual vigil commemorating the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown for roughly 30 years. Associated Press described the event as China’s only large-scale public commemoration of the crackdown. Chow and Lee were arrested on Sept. 8, 2021, charged the following day under Articles 22 and 23 of the security law, denied bail, and the Alliance dissolved later that month.

sections.heading: Court Ruling and Rights Concerns
sections.body: The court classified the offence as serious despite finding no violence, no specified method of implementation and no timetable for ending one-party rule, placing it in a statutory sentencing range of five to 10 years. It said the law had not been applied retrospectively and that the convictions rested on conduct during the charge period rather than ideology or pre-law conduct. Authorities maintain that the Alliance’s aim of ending Communist Party leadership sought to undermine China’s constitutional system, while UN mandate holders and the UK government have raised concerns about political expression and peaceful remembrance.

sections.heading: Sentences and Alliance Fine
sections.body: Chow was sentenced to seven years and three months, Lee to seven years, and Ho to five years and two months; the Alliance was fined HK$1.5 million. Ho’s lower sentence followed his guilty plea, while Lee and Chow pleaded not guilty. Police national-security chief superintendent Steve Li said the penalties should warn others against actions authorities regard as endangering national security.

explore_lenses.summary: The reported concern is not only that a chatbot can answer dangerous questions, but that coding and agentic systems can speed up planning, software development, reconnaissance and iterative testing. event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.

event_overview.title: About Midterm Elections
event_overview.subject: Midterm Elections
event_overview.summary: U.S. midterm elections are the regularly scheduled federal elections held in even-numbered years when no presidential election is on the ballot, choosing members of Congress and often coinciding with state and local contests. The 2026 general election is scheduled for November 3, with all House seats and one of the Senate’s three election classes at issue.

facts.label: Date
facts.value: The next regularly scheduled federal general election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026; federal law sets House elections for the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in every even-numbered year.

facts.label: House elections
facts.value: All 435 voting seats in the U.S. House of Representatives are contested every two years; representatives serve two-year terms.

facts.label: Senate elections
facts.value: Senators serve six-year terms divided into three classes, so approximately one-third of the Senate stands for election or reelection every two years.

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: Federal elections are administered primarily under state law, commonly by county or other local election authorities, subject to applicable federal requirements.

facts.label: Campaign-finance oversight
facts.value: The Federal Election Commission administers and enforces federal campaign-finance law for House and Senate campaigns, including disclosure rules and contribution and expenditure restrictions.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.summary: In September 2026, Jimmy Kimmel said an interview with Texas Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico would be released on the "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" YouTube channel rather than carried in the program’s ABC television broadcast. Kimmel described the decision as a response to what he said were FCC threats affecting the show, ABC, and local affiliates; the move highlighted how federal broadcast-election rules apply to licensed television stations but not to online distribution.

facts.label: Dates and release format
facts.value: Kimmel announced the change on September 9, 2026, and the interview was released online on September 10 rather than aired as part of the ABC broadcast.

facts.label: Participants
facts.value: The interview paired Jimmy Kimmel with James Talarico, who was reported as the Democratic candidate for Texas’s U.S. Senate seat and is also a sitting Texas House member representing District 50.

facts.label: News-program exception
facts.value: Section 315 excludes candidate appearances on bona fide newscasts, news interviews, qualifying documentaries, and on-the-spot news coverage from being treated as a candidate’s station “use”; FCC guidance has evaluated bona fide news interviews based on scheduling, producer control, and newsworthiness-based editorial judgment.

facts.label: Scope of the FCC rules at issue
facts.value: The statute addresses use of a “broadcasting station,” which is why the reported workaround used an online platform rather than the ABC broadcast feed; this does not itself resolve any dispute over the FCC’s authority or the applicability of an exemption to a particular program.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline covers the September 2026 decision to distribute this specific Kimmel–Talarico interview online and the stated FCC-related rationale, not the full Texas Senate campaign, all prior ABC–FCC disputes, or a legal adjudication of the parties’ competing claims.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.
